title: Harmonic and melodic minor
description: Memorize raised 6 and 7, the augmented second, and leading-tone resolutions on guitar.

cards.front: Give the formulas for natural, harmonic, and ascending melodic minor.
cards.back: Natural: 1 2 ♭3 4 5 ♭6 ♭7. Harmonic: 1 2 ♭3 4 5 ♭6 7 (raised 7). Melodic ascending: 1 2 ♭3 4 5 6 7 (raised 6 and 7).

cards.front: Spell natural, harmonic, and ascending melodic minor in A.
cards.back: Natural: A B C D E F G. Harmonic: A B C D E F G♯. Melodic ascending: A B C D E F♯ G♯.

cards.front: Do harmonic and melodic minor change the key signature?
cards.back: No. The signature stays natural minor (A minor has none). Raised notes appear as accidentals when needed.

cards.front: Why raise degree 7 in minor?
cards.back: In natural minor, 7 is a whole step below the tonic and v is minor, so pull to i is weak. Raising 7 makes a leading tone and a major V.

cards.front: In A minor, raise G to G♯. What two things happen?
cards.back: The V chord becomes major (E G♯ B), a stronger dominant. Degree 7 sits a half step below A and leads into it.

cards.front: What awkward interval does harmonic minor leave, and how large is it?
cards.back: An augmented second between ♭6 and 7. In A harmonic minor that is F to G♯: three half steps.

cards.front: Why raise 6 as well in melodic minor?
cards.back: It closes the gap: F♯ to G♯ is a whole step, so E F♯ G♯ A is smooth and stepwise.

cards.front: How do classical and jazz typically treat melodic minor direction?
cards.back: Classical: ascending form going up, natural minor going down (A G F E). Jazz often uses the ascending form both ways — vocabulary, not a rule of minor keys.

cards.front: On string 5 from open A, what frets are harmonic minor? Where is the three-fret gap?
cards.back: Frets 0 2 3 5 7 8 11 12. The gap from fret 8 (F) to fret 11 (G♯) is the augmented second.

cards.front: On string 5 from open A, what frets are ascending melodic minor? Name the notes.
cards.back: Frets 0 2 3 5 7 9 11 12: A B C D E F♯ G♯ A.

cards.front: On one string, how many frets are a whole step, a half step, and an augmented second?
cards.back: Whole step = 2 frets, half step = 1, augmented second = 3.

cards.front: In open E7 (020100) to Am (x02210), where is the leading-tone resolution?
cards.back: String 3: fret 1 is G♯, fret 2 is A. The leading tone resolves up a half step.

cards.front: Which open strings stay put from E7 to Am?
cards.back: Strings 2 and 1 stay open B and E. Those common tones hold still while string 3 moves G♯ → A.

cards.front: In D minor, where does the leading tone of A7 (x02020) resolve into Dm (xx0231)?
cards.back: String 2: fret 2 is C♯ in A7; fret 3 is D in Dm. That is C♯ → D.

cards.front: When does G♯ clash against a plain Am, and when is it the right note?
cards.back: Held against Am it is a major seventh above A and clashes, unless you want Am(maj7). Use it as a leading tone, a passing tone, or over E / E7, where it is the chord’s third.

cards.front: Spell natural, harmonic, and ascending melodic minor for E.
cards.back: Natural: E F♯ G A B C D. Harmonic: E F♯ G A B C D♯. Melodic: E F♯ G A B C♯ D♯.

cards.front: Spell D harmonic minor. Name the augmented second.
cards.back: D E F G A B♭ C♯. The augmented second is B♭ to C♯.

cards.front: Spell the V triad of A minor, D minor, and E minor from harmonic minor.
cards.back: E G♯ B, A C♯ E, B D♯ F♯.

cards.front: Compare Am – Em – Am with Am – E – Am. What is the difference?
cards.back: Em (v) has no leading tone, so the arrival is weak. E (V) has G♯ leading to A, so the cadence is stronger.

cards.front: In Am – Dm – E – Am, why is E major, and which scale supplies G♯?
cards.back: G♯ leads to A. The G♯ comes from harmonic minor; the key signature stays A minor.

cards.front: Does “minor uses harmonic minor” mean the whole tune switches scale?
cards.back: No. Raise 7, or 6 and 7, only where the music needs to lean into the tonic.
